## 7.1 A mobile OS is built in layers

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A mobile OS is a stack of layers between the hardware and the apps.
- Each layer uses only the services of the layer below it.
- The kernel runs on the hardware and manages processes, memory and drivers.
- **Do it:** Build both stacks in Stack Builder. Which iOS layer does the job of the Linux kernel?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/os-stack.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 1 · Layers

a) Which layer of a mobile OS runs directly on the hardware?
b) Which layers may each layer of the stack use?
c) Which jobs does the kernel do?

::: {.answer}
a) the kernel
b) only the layer below it
c) It manages processes, memory, drivers and power.
:::

## 7.2 Android and iOS

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Android has the Linux kernel, libraries, the app framework and the apps.
- iOS has Apple's own kernel, libraries, the app framework and the apps.
- Android runs on the phones of many makers, and iOS only on Apple's phones.
- **Do it:** Which OS does your phone run? Who made the phone, and who made the OS?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/android-ios.png)
:::
::::

## Example · One game, two builds

Byte Bay makes Pocket Quest in Unity for P5 (Android) and P8 (an iPhone).
**What does Byte Bay build for each phone?**

::: {.reveal}
1. For P5, an **.apk** package (an .aab for Google Play), drawn with Vulkan or OpenGL ES.
2. For P8, an **.ipa** package, built on a Mac and drawn with Metal.
3. The game code is the same, but each build uses the layers of its own OS.
:::

## Try it 2 · Android or iOS?

a) Which OS has the Linux kernel?
b) Which OS uses Metal for its graphics?
c) Can an iPhone install an .apk package?

::: {.answer}
a) Android
b) iOS
c) No, each platform needs its own build.
:::

## 7.3 Every app in its own sandbox

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A sandbox gives each app its own files and its own memory.
- An app cannot read the files of another app.
- An app reaches the camera, microphone or location only with a permission.
- **Do it:** Open the settings of a game. How much data does it use, and which permissions does it have?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/sandbox.png)
:::
::::

## Try it 3 · The sandbox

a) Pocket Quest wants the camera. Whom does it ask?
b) Can Pocket Quest read the files of the messages app?
c) What removes the saved progress of a game?

::: {.answer}
a) the OS
b) No, they are in another sandbox.
c) clearing its storage or deleting the app
:::

## 7.4 The life cycle of a game

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A game moves between foreground, background, suspended and ended.
- The OS tells the game before it leaves the foreground, so it can pause and save.
- When RAM is low, the OS ends apps in the background.
- **Do it:** Leave a game for a minute and come back. Did it continue or start again?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/app-lifecycle.png)
:::
::::

## Example · A message in level 2

Sara plays level 2 of a puzzle game, opens a message, and then opens many other apps.
**What happens to the game, and what does Sara see at the end?**

::: {.reveal}
1. The OS tells the game it leaves the foreground, and the game **stops the timer and saves**.
2. RAM gets low, so the OS **ends** the game in the background.
3. Sara taps the icon again, and the game loads the save: she is **back in level 2**.
:::

## Try it 4 · States

a) The game is on the screen and running. In which state is it?
b) The game is in RAM but gets no CPU time. In which state is it?
c) What must a game do when a call arrives?

::: {.answer}
a) foreground
b) suspended
c) pause and save
:::

## Try it 5 · Two phones (harder)

The facts: Rami tests Pocket Quest 1.2 on P5 (Android, 4 GB RAM) and on P8 (an iPhone). A call arrives in level 3, and later he opens ten other apps on P5.

a) Which package does Byte Bay build for the iPhone P8?
b) What does Android do with the game when RAM gets low on P5?
c) What does Rami see when he opens the game again?

::: {.answer}
a) an .ipa
b) It ends the game in the background.
c) level 3, loaded from the save
:::

## Summary

- A mobile OS is a stack of layers, from the kernel up to the apps.
- Android and iOS fill the same layers with different parts.
- Each platform needs its own build of the game.
- Every app lives in its own sandbox and needs permissions.
- A game must pause and save, because the OS may end it later.
